name: Python
title: Python (3.14)

presenceList.meta: R1, Ec8, Ec9, G3, Q2, Q3

preamble.text: Analysis against Python 3.14 (free-threaded mode officially supported).

type.text: **Duck typing**: Any object with a matching method name is accepted, so the interface a call expects is an assumption at the call site
**`match`/`case` is not exhaustive (3.10+)**: A value that matches no case falls through without an error, so completeness is the programmer's claim
**`|` union type syntax (3.10+)**: `str | int` cleaner than `Union[str, int]`
**Type hints (PEP 484) help**: Gradual typing, but not enforced by the runtime; `mypy`/`pyright` provide enforcement at build time
**Protocols (PEP 544) declare a structure for the type checker**: An object satisfies the protocol implicitly, and the runtime does not enforce it

construction.text: **`__init__` can have side effects**: Constructors couple to initialization
**Dataclasses decouple**: Auto-generated methods; `kw_only`, `slots` options improve control
**Multiple inheritance**: Diamond problem; MRO (Method Resolution Order) couples resolution to inheritance order
**`@override` decorator (3.12)**: Catches broken overrides at check time
**Global mutable state common**: Module-level variables couple
**Monkey patching couples**: Can modify anything at runtime
**Import side effects**: Module execution couples to import
**Mutable default arguments**: `def f(x=[])` couples calls together
**One value, many names**: names bind objects, and a parameter, a closure, and an attribute can hold the same list — assignment copies the name, never the value
The import system executes a module once, at first import; a circular import hands the importer the half-initialized module

memory.text: **Reference counting + GC**: Immediate deallocation for most objects
**No manual memory management**: Can't have use-after-free
**Reference cycles need GC**: Cycle detector runs periodically
**GC pauses affect latency**: Cycle collection can pause
**`__del__` timing non-deterministic**: Finalizers unreliable for resource cleanup
**Context managers cover the block they wrap**: `with` releases a resource at block exit, but a resource acquired outside one has no automatic release
**Global references common**: Module-level variables extend lifetimes

error.text: **Exceptions unchecked**: No type tracking in signatures
**Exception groups + `except*` (3.11+)**: Can handle multiple concurrent exceptions without losing information
**Broad exception catching couples**: `except Exception` catches too much
**Result types possible**: Libraries exist but not idiomatic
**A failure is not a value**: a `raise` cannot be folded into an expression, so each level rebuilds the `try`/`except` shape around the call

concurrency.text: **The GIL is still the default**: Free-threaded mode is opt-in through a `--disable-gil` build or the `python3.14t` executable, and threads then use multiple cores at a single-thread cost of about 5–10%
**Async functions are explicit**: `async def` marks which functions may suspend, so the boundary is visible at the declaration
**Multiprocessing decouples**: Separate processes, but manual (less necessary with free-threaded mode)
**Free-threaded mode is new**: Ecosystem still adapting; many C extensions need GIL

concurrency.prose: > **Note on concurrency:** Free-threaded mode (3.14+) is opt-in, so the default interpreter lock still charges `K1`: the analysis records the default a new project gets. A deployment that builds or installs the free-threaded variant removes that charge in deployment, and the score records the default.

platform.text: **No company owns the language**: Python is governed by the Python Software Foundation and released under the PSF Licence
**Several implementations exist**: CPython is the reference implementation, and PyPy, GraalPy, Jython, and IronPython are independent runtimes
**The runtime is portable**: CPython builds on Linux, macOS, Windows, and on many other platforms, including IBM z/OS
**The packaging tools are vendor-neutral**: Pip, venv, and the Python Package Index are not tied to one vendor's platform
**No vendor controls the roadmap**: Language changes are public Python Enhancement Proposals (PEPs) decided by the Steering Council

performance.text: **Slow**: Interpreted, dynamic (though free-threaded mode helps parallelism)
**Free-threaded mode**: Opt-in removal of GIL (3.14+); ~5–10% single-thread overhead
**C extensions help**: But couples to C ecosystem

ecosystem.text: **Excellent for data science**: NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn
**A wheel binds to an interpreter**: the filename names the Python, ABI, and platform tags, and the installer loads that binary [@pep425; @pep384]

**Stored byte-code binds to the release**: Python states that the marshal format is not guaranteed to be portable across Python versions and reserves the right to change it in non-backwards compatible ways, while the pickle format carries the published cross-release promise [@pyPickle]

reproducibility.text: **The contract the toolchain reads**: pip reads pyproject and requires-python, and the shipped tooling validates it against the running interpreter

supplychain.text: The PyPI name space is flat: one global namespace decides ownership.
The interpreter ships no package channel; pip and PyPI are the ecosystem's.

observability.text: The logging module ships handlers, formatters, and record fields in the standard library.
faulthandler and tracebacks ship by default, so a crash names its frames.

feedback.text: The compile-run loop answers in milliseconds with no build.
The standard distribution ships no analyzer; editor analysis rides third-party language servers.

governance.text: The PSF and the Steering Council run the language through public PEPs.

interop.text: ctypes and the C API ship in the standard library as the in-process foreign interface.
CPython is maintained for every common platform.

tradeoffs: **Free-threaded Mode vs. Ecosystem Readiness**: GIL removal is real but opt-in; many libraries haven't adapted
**Monkey Patching vs. the wrapper**: a live object can be repaired in place, and the repair must be repeated in every process that imports it
**Comprehensions vs. the loop**: an expression that builds a list hides the accumulation in one line, and a reader who needs the loop's control flow rewrites it
verdict: Python's duck typing provides maximum runtime flexibility but zero compile-time low coupling by language design. Free-threaded mode (3.14) eliminates the historical GIL concurrency coupling, though it's still opt-in. Pattern matching (3.10+) and exception groups (3.11+) improve error handling composition. Type checkers (mypy/pyright) provide static coupling detection at build time but not at runtime. Main strength: simplicity, ecosystem, libraries. Main weakness: all coupling invisible until runtime; runtime type safety depends on test coverage.

energy.text: Interpreted by default: the slowest class in the energy and time benchmarks [@pereira2017energy]; a causal re-analysis attributes most of the gap to execution time [@vankempen2025green].

ai-readiness.text: A large training corpus and strong code-generation results: models write this language well [@joel2025lowresource; @effibenchx2025].

safety.text: No certified or standards-qualified path is published for the language itself; a safety-critical deployment rests on a platform vendor's qualified runtime, not on the language.

delivery.note: A source distribution builds on the target machine
The wheel filename names the interpreter, ABI, and platform tags, and pip installs that binary

data_formats.note: Python publishes the promise for pickled data: the format is guaranteed backwards compatible across Python releases provided a compatible pickle protocol is chosen, and each protocol version is named for the release that first reads it

Python states that the marshal serialization format is not guaranteed to be portable across Python versions, and that the Python implementers reserve the right to change the serialization format in non-backwards compatible ways should the need arise
